scenes.title: 1971 Bristol School Cubicles: Klee vs Kandinsky Abstract Prints & Choosing '7-for-Us / 1-for-Them' Over '19-for-Us / 25-for-Them'!
scenes.era: 1971, Department of Psychology, University of Bristol, UK

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1971 British university room featuring two framed modernist abstract prints on an easel (**'Klee Group'** and **'Kandinsky Group'**), private wooden student desks, and a bold oversized **Tajfel Allocation Matrix Booklet** contrasting **Choice A (Max Joint Profit: 19 for Klee #47 / 25 for Kandinsky #23)** against **Choice B (Max Difference: 7 for Klee #47 / 1 for Kandinsky #23 — CIRCLED IN RED!)**.

positions.who: Henri Tajfel (mannequin in 1971 British tweed blazer, dark turtleneck/shirt, and spectacles)
positions.where: standing beside the Klee & Kandinsky easel holding the Matrix tally sheet in stunned fascination as boys sacrifice 12 points just to outscore the other painter label
positions.facing: standing beside art easel and matrix chart

positions.who: Two Bristol Schoolboy mannequins (in neat 1971 British school blazers and striped ties)
positions.where: seated in separate desks holding 'Group Klee' cards — firmly circling the **7-vs-1 Maximum Difference** box over the much richer **19-vs-25** box!

props.name: paired abstract modernist art prints ('Klee' & 'Kandinsky') + random group ID badges
props.period_detail: meaningless aesthetic labels assigned 100% at random

props.name: Tajfel Payoff Matrix Board ('19 / 25 Richer For Everyone [Skipped] vs 7 / 1 We Beat Them! [Chosen]')
props.period_detail: exposes relative-status tribalism with zero personal greed
props.physical_behavior: the smoking-gun number table of Social Identity Theory

actions.verb_sequence: hands each boy a private 'Member of Klee Group' slip after viewing the two abstract paintings -> Boys inspect the Payoff Matrix -> bypass the rich 19/25 column and decisively circle 7/1 so Klee finishes +6 ahead of Kandinsky!

reactions.reaction: shakes his head realizing there IS no 'zero baseline' once humans hear 'Us' and 'Them'
sit proudly having 'won' for Klee despite never meeting a single fellow Klee member

scenes.wardrobe: 1971 British attire: professor wool tweed jacket; 1971 British comprehensive-school navy blazers, white shirts, and striped school ties.
scenes.recognition_hook: Split schoolboys randomly by two abstract painters they've never heard of, and within five minutes they throw away 63% of their own team's money just so the other painter's group gets less!

key_visual.description: a 1971 Bristol psychology room with Klee and Kandinsky abstract prints beside schoolboys in blazers circling '7 vs 1' over '19 vs 25' on a large payoff matrix chart

scenes.title: 1973 Explicit Random Lottery: Even Pure Chance Creates a Tribe!

layout.description: Bright classroom table where an experimenter draws slips openly out of a clear glass bowl labeled 'Random Group X / Random Group W'.

positions.where: watching openly random Group X vs Group W assignments STILL produce clear in-group point favoritism

props.name: clear glass random-draw bowl ('Group X / Group W')
props.period_detail: removes even the illusion of shared artistic taste

actions.verb_sequence: draws Group X openly by chance -> Group X still awards more points to X than W

reactions.reaction: confirm bare linguistic categorization alone trips the switch

scenes.recognition_hook: Tell people straight to their faces their group label was picked out of a hat at random — and five minutes later they STILL favor their hat letter!

scenes.title: Corporate '7-vs-1' Silos: Sales vs Engineering Turf Wars

layout.description: Sunlit office split by two department banners ('Team Blue' vs 'Team Amber') hoarding information.

positions.where: holding back helpful data so their own department ranks #1 on quarterly slides while overall project launch lags

props.name: 19/25 Company Win vs 7/1 Department Ranking slide
props.period_detail: shows Tajfel's exact 1971 Bristol matrix happening inside Fortune 500 offices

actions.verb_sequence: spot the 7-vs-1 trap costing both teams

scenes.recognition_hook: Every time two company departments hoard credit so 'our silo wins' while the whole company loses, Bristol's 1971 schoolboys are running the meeting!

scenes.title: The Antidote: Cross-Cutting Shared Mission Teams

layout.description: Warm sunlit round oak table where engineers, designers, and marketers share one unified 'Launch Crew' badge and joint 19+25 scoreboard.

positions.where: collaborating openly around a round table selecting the 44-point Maximum Joint Profit outcome together

props.name: unified Common Ingroup badge & Joint Scoreboard
props.period_detail: harnesses Social Identity Theory FOR cooperation rather than zero-sum rivalry

actions.verb_sequence: combines pieces into one shared launch board -> everyone wins higher payout

scenes.recognition_hook: You can't delete the human tribal instinct — redraw the circle around a shared mission so 'Us' includes the whole table!
